### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json edecd44851675f68bd4fe9b93ddd7fc2640ef675`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **20** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json edecd44851675f68bd4fe9b93ddd7fc2640ef675` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ce00eeb64759ee1ba71f6d7b124c613d6a5dafe7` — the merge of head `eb0f825c75ba65cf63255aae7d69f11704c8a5ad` into base `edecd44851675f68bd4fe9b93ddd7fc2640ef675`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ce00eeb64759ee1ba71f6d7b124c613d6a5dafe7 && git checkout ce00eeb64759ee1ba71f6d7b124c613d6a5dafe7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin edecd44851675f68bd4fe9b93ddd7fc2640ef675 eb0f825c75ba65cf63255aae7d69f11704c8a5ad && git checkout -B drift-repro edecd44851675f68bd4fe9b93ddd7fc2640ef675 && git merge --no-ff eb0f825c75ba65cf63255aae7d69f11704c8a5ad

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json edecd44851675f68bd4fe9b93ddd7fc2640ef675
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs edecd44851675f68bd4fe9b93ddd7fc2640ef675` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f2591d6b15ca31e397f9dc4a1e68bad5293e1f95`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-12T05:34Z, adversarially, against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12 and Post-Task Checklist step 3. Inputs: card #15953 (body and all 10 comments: the classification table `6115219467`, slice 1's landed note `6116484972`, the slice 2 claim `6117164426`, the dev report `6118182405`, the seat's ACCEPT `6118237845`, read as a claim); PR #22953 body, file list and the net diff of `refs/pull/22953/head` against merge base `e357a441c6` (10 files, +1321 / -9); the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The three functions and nine types, reachable and coherent: right.** `packages/verify/package.json` maps `.` to `dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts` (and the `require` pair), and `packages/verify/src/index.ts` exports `deriveDeleteBehaviorCases`, `runDeleteBehaviorProofs`, `formatDeleteBehaviorReport` and the nine types from `./delete-behavior.js`, so every one is reachable through the published entry. Shapes mirror the family beside them: `deriveXCases(config)` / `runXProofs(stack, token, config, { doors? })` / `formatXReport(report)` is exactly `deriveReferenceShapeCases` / `runReferenceShapeProofs` / `formatReferenceShapeReport`; `summary.hardFailures` is the gate count as in `ReferenceShapeReport` and `RlsReport`; `app` is computed by the same expression. The status vocabulary differs where the meaning differs (`contradicted` for a declaration a delete did something else to, where reference-shape says `holes`; `not-derivable` split out of `excluded` so "the declaration states no outcome" and "no fixture can be built" are not one bucket), and each value's docblock matches `fieldStatus` and `judge` line for line. One docblock promise is slightly wider than the code: `runDeleteBehaviorProofs` says it "never throws on a per-field failure"; the fixture create, the REST delete and the system delete are each caught, but the three `stack.rows` read-backs are not, so a harness-level read fault would escape rather than land as `failed`. Not a contract defect (the same is true of the sibling families, and a read fault is a harness fault, not a field verdict); noted, not flagged.

**`os verify --delete-behaviors`: right.** `Flags.boolean` with `default: false`; the flag is typed into `runVerification`'s parameter and `this.parse(Verify)` hands `flags` through whole. With the flag, `bootStack(config, { multiTenant, hostRoot })` is a fresh stack stopped in `finally`, `deleteBehaviors.summary.hardFailures` is added to `hardFailures` under `?? 0`, and `deleteBehaviors` rides `emitJson` (a `JSON.stringify`, so an `undefined` value emits no key). Without the flag nothing moves: `hardFailures` adds 0, the text branch is `if (deleteBehaviors)`, the `--json` document carries no `deleteBehaviors` key, and the exit status reads what it read. The CLI pin `packages/cli/test/verify-delete-behaviors.test.ts` holds exactly that (`'deleteBehaviors' in doc` is false, exit 0 without the flag; exit 0 / 1 with it on the proven and control apps), spawned so the exit status is real. The only thing that moves for every caller is help text: the command `description` and one `examples` row name the new flag. That is a widening, carried by the minor.

**The expectation's source: right, and the exclusions are exclusions, not models.** `deriveDeleteBehaviorCases` takes `declared` from `FieldSchema.safeParse(def).data.deleteBehavior` and from nowhere else; `judge` reads `c.declared` and the rows the engine left, and no code path assigns a behaviour. Checked against the spec at the head: the `.overwrite` at `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (about line 2764) materializes `set_null` only on `lookup` and `tree`, keeps an authored value verbatim, leaves a bare `master_detail` and a `user` without the key, and the `superRefine` (about line 2619) refuses an authored `set_null` on `master_detail`. What each value means is the enum's own meta and the field reference (`content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx` rows 312 and 334). The three shapes the claim forbade copying are each excluded with the reason and given no expectation: a `set_null` on a required reference (the escalation rule), a field whose parse carries no key (the `master_detail` default, and `user`), and the per-row multi rule falls under the first because the `required` test is on the field whatever `multiple` says. A parse refusal and an unreadable target are excluded with the issue. The family's own test pins all of it (`dbp_bare.parent`, `dbp_required.parent`, `dbp_holder.assignee` excluded; the `x_child.parent` parse refusal named). A consequence worth stating plainly: a `tree` field's materialized `set_null` IS compared, the engine's `cascadeRelationBehavior` walks `master_detail` and `lookup` only (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, about line 17806), and the family therefore reports the showcase's `f_tree` contradicted. That is the card's rule working as written (declared, not enforced, so a finding), not the family modelling the engine's guard.

**Attribution: right.** `refusedHere` is `answer.kind === 'refused' && code === 'DELETE_RESTRICTED' && dependentObject === c.object && (object === undefined || object === c.target)`. The engine sets `err.code = 'DELETE_RESTRICTED'`, `err.object` (the target) and `err.dependentObject = childName` (the machine name, not the rendered label) at about line 18266 to 18273, which is the structured half of the ADR-0112 envelope. A `restrict` reads `held` only on that refusal with the target and holder both still present and the holder still referencing the target; any other refusal is `unattributed` and the field `inconclusive`, never `proven`. No prose is parsed. The attribution control (`nc_vault` refusing every delete with its own `VALIDATION_FAILED`) pins that a vetoed `restrict` and a vetoed `cascade` both read `inconclusive`. A `DELETE_RESTRICTED` whose `object` names a different object than the probed target reads unattributed, which errs toward inconclusive, the safe side. A refusal naming this relation on a declared `cascade` or `set_null` reads `contradicted`, which is also right: by construction no other field of the probe holder references the probe target (required references are filled from the base record, not from `t`).

**The `CALLERS` row (`not-a-served-read`): true of the code.** `delete-behavior.ts` calls `referenceTargetOf` to name the target object; it creates target and holder records through `POST /data/OBJECT` where that object is the addressed one, deletes the target through `DELETE /data/TARGET/ID` and `hooks.run(target, 'delete', { id }, { system: true })`, and reads rows back through `stack.rows(object, { id })` with no caller, which `handle.ts` resolves to `SYSTEM_CONTEXT`. The report carries the holder's field value and object names, never a field of the target. The row's text says exactly that, and the pin's own scan (every non-test caller classified, every classified file still calling) is what turned red before the row.

**The two `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows: true of the code.** The gate's candidate is an exported function whose parameter 0 is annotated with an interface declared in the package and re-exported as a type from its index. `runDeleteBehaviorProofs(stack: VerifyStack, ...)` and `formatDeleteBehaviorReport(report: DeleteBehaviorReport)` are exactly those two; `deriveDeleteBehaviorCases(config: any)` is not a candidate. `VerifyStack` is the concrete handle `bootStack` returns and `DeleteBehaviorReport` is a value this package produced, so neither is a surface an out-of-tree implementer provides. The rows are the gate's prescribed remedy and the reasons are the same words the sibling rows use.

**Docs and changeset sentences against the diff: right.** `packages/verify/README.md`: "Four app-agnostic proof families" (CRUD, RLS, reference shape, delete behaviour), the bullet, the exit-code sentence (`contradicted` or `failed` fail the run; inconclusive, excluded and not-derivable do not), the status table and the API line all match `delete-behavior.ts`. `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`: the example row, the paragraph in the `os verify` section only, and the `--json` key list (`deleteBehaviors` with the flag) match `verify.ts`. The changeset's export list is the full set (3 functions, 9 types), its signature line is the real one, and its sentence that a `tree` field's delete is not honoured today is accurate at this head: the spec materializes `set_null` on `tree`, the engine's walk never reaches a `tree` field, and the seat filed it as #22957 (open, `finding`), which names the producer `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/field-zoo.object.ts:117` and both doors. That sentence ships in `CHANGELOG.md` and is time-bound by "today": whichever PR repairs #22957 owes it an edit if this changeset is still pending then, as the ACCEPT already records.

**First-consumer evidence (hotcrm): consistent with the retired pins.** Rows 1 to 3's D halves: 5 of the 7 end-to-end cascades proven, 0 contradictions on any reached field, the two unreached named with reasons that are the app's (an attendee rule the generic fixture cannot satisfy; a `sys_user` target). The excluded `crm_campaign`, `crm_event` and `crm_product` are the table's own K and R residues (required `set_null`). The evidence came from direct runs of the family, not from `os verify`; see ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15953-verify-delete-behavior-family.md`: `@objectstack/verify` **minor**, `@objectstack/cli` **minor**. The diff publishes three new functions and nine new types from `@objectstack/verify` and one new opt-in flag plus help text from `@objectstack/cli`; it removes and renames nothing, narrows no accept set, and changes no default. Minor is the right level for both, and it meets the card's own acceptance ("`@objectstack/verify` minor per new exported family"). Not breaking, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed; `Check Changeset` on the head is green and the dev's local `check-adr-0087-registration` read "no declared-breaking changeset".

`Clause-②` carriers: PR body line 2 `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset body `Clause-②: yes`; the claim comment `6117164426` `Clause-②: yes`. The three agree. Each is legal: `yes` with no arm is a declaration (the arm is optional, and `yes (widening)` would add nothing), and `yes` takes at least minor, which both entries are.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6118182405`: `open_questions` is empty, so nothing to answer there. Its deviations and findings, each answered or escalated:

- **Both conditional surfaces used** (2 `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows, 1 `CALLERS` row): each because its gate went red first, within the claim's conditional clause, logic untouched. Answered in ① as true classifications.
- **The family's own `fixtureBody`** instead of slice 1's module-private helper: `reference-shape.ts` is outside the claim's surface, and the cut-down body changes which fixtures the app accepts, not what the comparison judges (the judgement is `judge`, which reads only the declaration and the rows). Answered.
- **A merge of `origin/main`** (`e357a441c6`, no conflicts, no force-push): the head is a merge commit whose net diff is the 10 files reviewed. Answered.
- **hotcrm evidence by direct runs, not `os verify`**: this tree is protocol 18 and hotcrm pins `^17.7.0`, so the card's clause "runs from `os verify` on hotcrm's metadata" cannot be met on this tree for this slice either. ESCALATED, not a FAIL: it is the same open acceptance note slice 1 landed under (`6116484972`), the card stays open for its remaining rows, and whoever closes the card owes that clause a run or a re-scope. The three readings (A on 17.7.0 REST-only, B migrated with hooks grafted, C hooks inert) agree on 0 contradictions.
- **One non-run ablation attempt**: reported as a non-run and replaced by a landed mutation (anchor 1 to 0, red `2 failed`, restore proven, green), repeated on the final head. Answered.
- **Commit trailers in AGENTS.md's model-free form**: a process note, not a contract matter. Answered.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1** (`tree` `deleteBehavior` not honoured, class b, public door): filed by the seat as #22957. Answered; the family stays opt-in until it is repaired, and the docs say so.
- **Out-of-scope findings 2 and 3, no carrier**: (2) a `set_null` clear that faults a holder's traversing validation rule is refused as `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the relation in prose only, so the family reports `inconclusive` (showcase `showcase_invoice.contact`). Under #10 this is not a reproducible defect: the engine fails closed, which is correct, and no contract names a structured relation on that refusal; a note is the right carrier. ESCALATED to the seat only as a choice: if it wants the envelope to carry a structured `dependentObject` there so the family can attribute it, that is a card of its own, not this PR's. (3) a generic fixture cannot satisfy every app rule (a term tied to a date range, a type select naming the probed party): an app fact, reported `inconclusive` with the app's own refusal, never `proven`. A note is right. Answered.

**Check-runs on the head, read five times in this act, the last just before posting (latest run per name).** Concluded success: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and its three shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the four PR-shape guards, `Spec property liveness`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `(2/6)` and `(5/6)`, the four `Type Check` jobs, `TypeScript Type Check` and `filter`. Roster skips: `Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`. Still in progress at the last read: `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:verify-stand-in`) and `Test Core (3/6)` and `(4/6)` (the shards that carry the cli integration tier and the core `repo` project with the `#22661` pin sit somewhere in the six). Judged on what concluded.

**One concluded red, read and attributed: `Test Core (6/6)`, conclusion `failure`.** ESCALATED, and it is the one item that stands between this record and the queue. What the job says about itself: step 12 "Run this shard's tests" is success, and step 15 "Test completeness guard" reads `12 of 12 scheduled package(s) reported, 20122 test(s) declared and all accounted for`; the red is step 14 "Check this shard's timing drift" alone: `shard-timing-drift: DRIFT, 2955.2s measured vs 1849.4s predicted across 12 package(s) = 1.60x (warning past 1.3x, red past 1.5x)`, heaviest overshoots `@objectstack/runtime` 1.73x, `@objectstack/service-analytics` 2.21x, `@objectstack/rest` 1.45x, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` 1.72x, `@objectstack/client` 1.63x. None of those five is in this diff, and the overshoot is uniform across them, which is the signature of a slow runner, not of a test this PR added. The same check was success on `origin/main` for the six latest commits, the newest run started two minutes before this one, and `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` was refreshed on main earlier this day (#22923), so this is not a standing red. The gate's own remedy text names the dataset refresh lane and forbids absorbing the gap in a PR ("do NOT hand-edit the dataset or raise this bound"), so nothing in this diff is owed or allowed as a fix. Limits of this reading, stated: the readable tail of the job log (5338 lines) names only the five packages above; the head of the log, where the shard's package set is printed, and the uploaded artifacts are beyond this reader's reach, so whether a `cli`, `verify` or `core` slice sits on that shard was not read. It does not move the verdict: the test step passed whole, and a slice of this diff's packages could not have put five untouched packages 1.45x to 2.21x over their predictions. No gate was re-run by this act. What the seat owes before the queue: a green latest run of `Test Core (6/6)` on this head (a re-run of that job, which is the seat's act, and the latest run of the name is what the tier reads), and green conclusions on the four still in progress. A red that reproduces on the re-run at or past 1.5x is the dataset's, filed to the refresh lane as #22923 was, and the landing waits on it; a red of any other kind on this head needs a new record.
